title: A Movement to Fight Misinformation... With Misinformation

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Annie Correal.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的安妮·科雷尔。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A new movement is underway to confront the growing threat of misinformation by creating misinformation.
sentences.zh: 一场新的运动正在兴起，旨在通过制造虚假信息来对抗日益严重的虚假信息威胁。

sentences.en: Today, the improbable story of the group behind that movement.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲述这股运动背后的群体的不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: Birds aren't real.
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Taylor Lorenz.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事泰勒·洛伦兹。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, February 9th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月9日，星期三。

sentences.en: Hi, Taylor.
sentences.zh: 你好，泰勒。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Hi, I'm good.
sentences.zh: 你好，我很好。

sentences.en: So, when you published this article back in December on Birds Aren't Real, it was probably the first time that a lot of people had ever heard of this quote-unquote conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 那么，当你在去年12月发表关于“鸟不是真的”这篇文章时，这可能是很多人第一次听说这个所谓的“阴谋论”。

sentences.en: It certainly was the first time I had heard of it.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我第一次听说。

sentences.en: So, at a very basic level, what is Birds Aren't Real?
sentences.zh: 那么，从最基础的层面来说，“鸟不是真的”到底是什么？

sentences.en: Birds Aren't Real is a fake conspiracy movement, mostly supported by young people online, that purports that birds are not real,
sentences.zh: “鸟不是真的”是一个虚假的阴谋论运动，主要由网上的年轻人支持，它声称鸟类不是真实的，

sentences.en: but were actually replaced by government drones back in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 而是实际上在20世纪70年代被政府的无人机所取代了。

sentences.en: In the conspiracy lore, every bird is actually a surveillance tool by the state.
sentences.zh: 在阴谋论的传说中，每一只鸟实际上都是国家的一种监控工具。

sentences.en: That's pretty funny.
sentences.zh: 那挺有趣的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's a parody conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个恶搞阴谋论。

sentences.en: It's almost a satire social movement.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是一场讽刺性的社会运动。

sentences.en: People know that this is not real.
sentences.zh: 人们知道这不是真的。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So then, why did you get interested in covering this?
sentences.zh: 那么，你为什么会对报道这个感兴趣呢？

sentences.en: I mean, things do come and go a lot on the internet, and it sounds like no one really believes in this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，互联网上的东西来来去去，听起来并没有人真的相信这个。

sentences.en: So, why in your mind was this fake conspiracy worth reporting on?
sentences.zh: 所以，在你看来，为什么这个虚假的阴谋论值得报道？

sentences.en: So, as an internet culture writer, I'm constantly keeping an eye on new trends, and they do come and go.
sentences.zh: 作为一名互联网文化撰稿人，我一直在关注新的趋势，它们确实来来去去。

sentences.en: But this one really had staying power, and it seemed to speak to something deep within the psyche of Gen Z.
sentences.zh: 但这个运动确实有持久力，而且它似乎触及了Z世代内心深处的东西。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I just noticed that the followers were very young and very dedicated, and their movement was manifesting increasingly in the real world.
sentences.zh: 我只是注意到追随者非常年轻且非常投入，他们的运动越来越多地在现实世界中显现出来。

sentences.en: Birds aren't real!
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的！

sentences.en: Birds aren't real!
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的！

sentences.en: Birds aren't real!
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的！

sentences.en: What stuck out to me was this huge protest that they organized outside Twitter's headquarters in San Francisco last November.
sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的是去年11月他们在旧金山推特总部外组织的那场大规模抗议活动。

sentences.en: To protest the bird logo.
sentences.zh: 为了抗议那只鸟的标志。

sentences.en: This is about government spying on all of us, taking away our freedoms, our privacy, and, like, telling us what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 这是关于政府在监视我们所有人，剥夺我们的自由、隐私，就像是在告诉我们该做什么一样。

sentences.en: I was like, oh my God, there's so many of them, and they were screaming with megaphones.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，他们有这么多人，而且他们拿着扩音器在尖叫。

sentences.en: We're about to march on Twitter headquarters three times like it's Jericho.
sentences.zh: 我们要像耶利哥城一样，绕着推特总部游行三次。

sentences.en: Birds aren't real!
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的！

sentences.en: Birds aren't real!
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的！

sentences.en: There's also been dozens of rallies on college campuses across the country in the past year.
sentences.zh: 过去一年里，全国各地的大学校园里也举行了数十场集会。

sentences.en: It just sort of started to enter into mainstream youth culture in a way that it hadn't in years prior.
sentences.zh: 它开始以一种前几年没有的方式进入主流青年文化。

sentences.en: Mm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I started to think, I've got to get to the bottom of how this started and why it seems to resonate so deeply with Gen Z.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始想，我必须弄清楚它是如何开始的，以及为什么它似乎与Z世代产生如此深刻的共鸣。

sentences.en: The problem is that the leader of birds aren't real is a bit of a troll.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，“鸟不是真的”的领导者有点像个喷子。

sentences.en: I consider myself to be an average American.
sentences.zh: 我自认为是一个普通的美国人。

sentences.en: I wake up in the morning, wash my car, and I have an avid disbelief in avian beings.
sentences.zh: 我早上起床，洗车，并且对鸟类生物有着狂热的不信任。

sentences.en: He would give these interviews where he's in character and fully embodying this conspiracy with a totally straight face.
sentences.zh: 他会接受这些采访，在采访中他完全进入角色，一本正经地体现这个阴谋论。

sentences.en: So how did you become aware of it?
sentences.zh: 那么你是怎么知道它的呢？

sentences.en: What is the message of the movement?
sentences.zh: 这个运动传达的信息是什么？

sentences.en: The message of the movement is essentially to spread awareness that from 1959 through 2001, the government mercilessly genocided over 12 billion birds
sentences.zh: 这个运动传达的信息本质上是传播一种意识：从1959年到2001年，政府无情地屠杀了超过120亿只鸟，

sentences.en: and simultaneously replaced them with surveillance drones in disguise that film us every day.
sentences.zh: 并同时用伪装的监控无人机取代了它们，每天都在拍摄我们。

sentences.en: So I thought, okay, how am I going to get to the bottom of birds aren't real if the founder is playing this character all the time?
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，好吧，如果创始人一直扮演这个角色，我该如何弄清“鸟不是真的”的真相呢？

sentences.en: But after years of covering internet and youth culture and having so many sources in this world, I finally got in touch with him.
sentences.zh: 但在报道互联网和青年文化多年，并在这一领域拥有如此多消息来源之后，我终于联系上了他。

sentences.en: I talked to him off the record, and then finally he agreed to go on the record, out of character, as himself.
sentences.zh: 我私下和他谈过，最后他同意正式接受采访，脱离角色，以他自己的身份。

sentences.en: Is this still recording?
sentences.zh: 还在录音吗？

sentences.en: Oh yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，在录着。

sentences.en: And yes, we are still running.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们还在运行。

sentences.en: Okay, awesome.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: So can I ask, how do you feel recorded as yourself?
sentences.zh: 那么我可以问一下，以你自己的身份被记录是什么感觉吗？

sentences.en: It feels really vulnerable, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，感觉真的很脆弱。

sentences.en: His name is Peter McIndoo, and he's a 23-year-old college dropout.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫彼得·麦金杜，是一名23岁的大学辍学生。

sentences.en: And in talking to him, it turns out that his background actually has a lot to do with how Birds Aren't Real got started.
sentences.zh: 在与他交谈中，事实证明他的背景实际上与“鸟不是真的”是如何开始的有很大关系。

sentences.en: I just remember basically growing up feeling like we were these, like, outsiders in the world.
sentences.zh: 我只记得基本上是在感觉我们是这个世界上的局外人中长大的。

sentences.en: He grew up in a pretty conservative and religious community with seven siblings outside Cincinnati, and then he moved to rural Arkansas.
sentences.zh: 他在辛辛那提郊外一个相当保守和宗教的社区长大，有七个兄弟姐妹，后来搬到了阿肯色州的农村。

sentences.en: Because my dad was going to go work in ministry.
sentences.zh: 因为我父亲要去从事牧师工作。

sentences.en: He was homeschooled.
sentences.zh: 他是接受家庭教育长大的。

sentences.en: I remember being told that a big reason we were being homeschooled was to protect us from these kind of massive brainwashing schemes that were in place by the government.
sentences.zh: 我记得有人告诉我，我们接受家庭教育的一个重要原因是保护我们免受政府实施的这种大规模洗脑计划的伤害。

sentences.en: So, like, evolution, for instance, or homosexuality, these concepts, are part of this grander government scheme to, like, corrupt the soul of the nation.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如进化论，或者同性恋，这些概念都是政府腐蚀国家灵魂的更大阴谋的一部分。

sentences.en: But he said that from a young age, he started to realize he was a little bit different from the rest of his community.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，从很小的时候起，他就开始意识到自己与社区里的其他人有点不同。

sentences.en: So, for instance, he told me a story about one time when he said that he didn't believe in God.
sentences.zh: 例如，他给我讲了一个故事，有一次他说他不相信上帝。

sentences.en: I was 10 years old, and I told my pastor at church, the youth group pastor, that I was the kind of Christian who went to church but didn't believe in God.
sentences.zh: 我当时10岁，我告诉教堂里的牧师，那个青年组的牧师，说我是一个去教堂但不相信上帝的基督徒。

sentences.en: Because I was so young, I didn't even realize that that, like, wasn't even a Christian.
sentences.zh: 因为我太小了，我甚至没有意识到那甚至算不上基督徒。

sentences.en: And I was told I was possessed with a demon, which is, like, crazy.
sentences.zh: 然后我被告知我被恶魔附身了，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And was told the devil had gotten a hold of him, essentially.
sentences.zh: 基本上被告知魔鬼已经控制了他。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He's a black sheep.
sentences.zh: 他是家里的害群之马。

sentences.en: And so, starting at 10 years old, I was kind of, like, exiled in some different ways from these homeschool communities.
sentences.zh: 所以，从10岁开始，我就在某种程度上被这些家庭教育社区流放了。

sentences.en: It was very much, like, the problem.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上就像是问题所在。

sentences.en: Like, in homeschool homecoming, for instance, they, like, voted people certain things for the year.
sentences.zh: 比如，在家庭教育返校节上，他们会投票选出年度人物。

sentences.en: Like, you know, you're, you know, you're going to be the most successful.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，你将会是最成功的。

sentences.en: I was voted most likely to go to jail.
sentences.zh: 我被投票选为最可能坐牢的人。

sentences.en: Which led to just, like, an entire childhood of, like, I guess you could call it, like, ideological loneliness.
sentences.zh: 这导致了整个童年时期，我想你可以称之为意识形态上的孤独。

sentences.en: Like, that must have been so hard.
sentences.zh: 那一定很艰难。

sentences.en: I mean, where did you turn when you felt that loneliness?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你感到孤独时，你转向了哪里？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll tell people that I was, like, raised by the internet.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会告诉人们我是被互联网养大的。

sentences.en: So, he increasingly went and turned to the internet.
sentences.zh: 所以，他越来越多地转向了互联网。

sentences.en: And ended up just, like, getting on YouTube and, like, Reddit and these other things.
sentences.zh: 最后只是上了YouTube、Reddit和这些其他东西。

sentences.en: And then, like, just searching things on my own.
sentences.zh: 然后，只是自己搜索东西。

sentences.en: And realizing that, like, the world did not think, like, this community that I was in thinks.
sentences.zh: 并意识到世界并不像我所在的这个社区那样思考。

sentences.en: It was kind of those places that let him see the outside world and helped him gain more perspective on the situation that he was in.
sentences.zh: 正是这些地方让他看到了外面的世界，并帮助他对所处的环境有了更多的认识。

sentences.en: Which is interesting, because I think we often think about conspiratorial thinking thriving on the internet.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我认为我们经常认为阴谋论思维在互联网上盛行。

sentences.en: And it does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But for Peter, it's actually his real life that feels dominated by conspiracy and the internet that feels like real life.
sentences.zh: 但对彼得来说，实际上是他的现实生活感觉被阴谋所主导，而互联网感觉像是真实的生活。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So, from Peter's point of view, he couldn't get away from homeschool fast enough to leave for college,
sentences.zh: 所以，从彼得的角度来看，他迫不及待地想离开家庭教育去上大学，

sentences.en: which he finally did in 2016 when he ended up at the University of Arkansas in Fayetteville.
sentences.zh: 他终于在2016年做到了，当时他进入了位于费耶特维尔的阿肯色大学。

sentences.en: And that's where I was really able to, like, break away and start kind of my own life.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那里，我真的能够摆脱束缚，开始我自己的生活。

sentences.en: And so, tell me about that day, that first day when Birds Aren't Real started.
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉我那一天，也就是“鸟不是真的”开始的第一天。

sentences.en: So, I was just visiting Memphis for, like, 24 hours and was in a really weird state of mind.
sentences.zh: 当时我只是去孟菲斯待了24小时，精神状态非常奇怪。

sentences.en: I had just, like, gotten cheated on by my girlfriend and was really, like, upset.
sentences.zh: 我刚被女朋友劈腿，真的很心烦。

sentences.en: So, I went to Memphis and there was a rally happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了孟菲斯，那里正好有一场集会。

sentences.en: Like, there were all these people with signs.
sentences.zh: 就像，有很多人拿着标语牌。

sentences.en: At one point, he goes to visit a friend in Memphis in 2017.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他在2017年去孟菲斯探望朋友。

sentences.en: It's January, right after Trump was elected, and there's a huge women's march downtown.
sentences.zh: 那是1月，就在特朗普当选后，市中心有一场大规模的女性游行。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was just looking down and noticed there were, like, counter-protesters there, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我只是往下看，注意到那里也有反抗议者。

sentences.en: Along with that women's march, there was also counter-protesters.
sentences.zh: 除了那场女性游行，还有反抗议者。

sentences.en: So, pro-Trump protesters shouting at the women's march.
sentences.zh: 也就是支持特朗普的抗议者在对女性游行队伍大喊大叫。

sentences.en: There were just, like, arguments forming.
sentences.zh: 争论正在形成。

sentences.en: Like, there were clearly, it's like, body language type stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像，很明显，这是肢体语言之类的事情。

sentences.en: Like, you could tell there were probleMs.
sentences.zh: 就像，你能看出有问题。

sentences.en: So, he's watching all of this chaos unfold in front of him and just the tension in the air.
sentences.zh: 所以，他看着眼前发生的所有混乱，感受着空气中的紧张气氛。

sentences.en: I thought about how funny, like, a skit would be if someone had a sign at a rally that had nothing to do with the rally.
sentences.zh: 我想如果有人在集会上举着一个与集会毫无关系的标语牌，那该多滑稽。

sentences.en: Thinking of, like, an archetype of a character that would be, like, just as energetically representing his beliefs.
sentences.zh: 想到一个角色的原型，他会以同样充满活力的方式代表他的信仰。

sentences.en: But they just meant nothing.
sentences.zh: 但它们毫无意义。

sentences.en: Like, it just meant just pointing to something absurd.
sentences.zh: 就像，这只是指向一些荒谬的东西。

sentences.en: And so, ended up finding a poster on a wall for, like, an event that had already passed.
sentences.zh: 于是，最后在墙上发现了一张已经过期的活动海报。

sentences.en: And the back of the poster was all just, like, white.
sentences.zh: 海报的背面全是白色的。

sentences.en: And so, took the poster off the wall.
sentences.zh: 于是，把海报从墙上撕了下来。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: He decides to rip a poster off the street and write...
sentences.zh: 他决定从街上撕下一张海报，写上……

sentences.en: And just writing the three most random words I could think of, which were, birds aren't real.
sentences.zh: 然后写下了我能想到的最随机的三个词，那就是：鸟不是真的。

sentences.en: Birds aren't real.
sentences.zh: 鸟不是真的。

sentences.en: And they didn't mean anything at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时它们没有任何意义。

sentences.en: It was just three random words.
sentences.zh: 那只是三个随机的词。

sentences.en: Then I picked up the sign and just started marching around with the people.
sentences.zh: 然后我拿起牌子，开始和人们一起游行。

sentences.en: And then he joined the counter-protest to the women's march and started chanting, birds aren't real, and holding up his sign.
sentences.zh: 然后他加入了针对女性游行的反抗议活动，开始高喊“鸟不是真的”，并举着他的牌子。

sentences.en: So, as I marched around, people would ask me, like, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 所以，当我游行时，人们会问我，那是什么意思？

sentences.en: And I had to just kind of come up with something on the spot.
sentences.zh: 我不得不当场编造一些东西。

sentences.en: And so, I didn't even really think about it too hard.
sentences.zh: 所以，我甚至没有太认真地去想它。

sentences.en: I just started talking about how I was a part of a movement that had been around for 50 years.
sentences.zh: 我只是开始说我是这个已经存在了50年的运动的一部分。

sentences.en: And that, you know, we're telling people that every bird in the skies is a government surveillance drone.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们告诉人们天上的每一只鸟都是政府的监控无人机。

sentences.en: I think I just watched, like, an Edward Snowden documentary or something.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时刚看过爱德华·斯诺登的纪录片之类的东西。

sentences.en: So, it was like, I had assumed this alternate identity that day and kind of unintentionally ended up being this person very similar to the people I grew up around.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像那天我假设了一个替代身份，无意中成了这个与我成长环境中的人非常相似的人。

sentences.en: And so, as...
sentences.zh: 所以，当……

sentences.en: And it wasn't really intended to be anything, but a woman had actually been filming him that day, unbeknownst to him.
sentences.zh: 这本来没打算成为什么，但那天确实有一个女人在拍他，他自己却不知道。

sentences.en: And she put that video on Facebook.

sentences.zh: 政府刚刚给它们进行了固件更新，使它们能够通过注视你来窃取你的信用卡信息

sentences.zh: 这些帖子开始在全国范围内获得关注。

sentences.en: Peter gets together with some friends.
sentences.zh: 彼得和一些朋友聚在一起。

sentences.en: They start posting videos where he's in character and building out the lore of Birds Aren't Real even more.
sentences.zh: 他们开始发布视频，他在视频中扮演角色，进一步构建“鸟类不是真的”的传说。

sentences.en: Welcome to Bird History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到鸟类历史。

sentences.en: I remember seeing these on my feed.
sentences.zh: 我记得在我的信息流里看到过这些。

sentences.en: It all began in 1946, when government accountability was at its lowest after a rampant rise of nationalism.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于 1946 年，当时民族主义猖獗，政府的问责制降到了最低点。

sentences.zh: 他揭示了政府是如何让鸟类看起来是真的。

sentences.zh: 政府在全国每个鸡窝下都安装了管道。

sentences.en: But Bill, how will they keep their batteries charged?

sentences.en: We'll string wires between them.
sentences.zh: 在它们之间架设电线。

sentences.en: All they gotta do is land them.
sentences.zh: 它们只需要落上去就行了。

sentences.en: So, Peter and his friends are really leaning in.
sentences.zh: 所以，彼得和他的朋友们真的投入进去了。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: As always, stay woke, patriots.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，保持清醒，爱国者们。

sentences.en: Birds aren't real.

sentences.zh: 然后他们开始制作越来越精致的视频。

sentences.en: I know we talked off camera some, but just for our viewers who don't know much about you, can you give us some on your background?
sentences.zh: 我知道我们私下聊过一些，但对于那些不太了解你的观众，你能介绍一下你的背景吗？

sentences.en: I was doing security for the CIA.
sentences.zh: 我曾为中情局做安保工作。

sentences.en: I was in D.C.
sentences.zh: 我在华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: At one point, he hired an actor to portray a former CIA agent.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他雇了一名演员来扮演一名前中情局特工。

sentences.en: And it's while I was there that,
sentences.zh: 就在我在那儿的时候，

sentences.en: well, I saw some things that I really wish I hadn't seen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我看到了一些我真希望自己没看到的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And if Peter starts amassing a real following and fan base, thousands of people are watching and sharing all of his videos and posts it becomes this viral phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 随着彼得开始积累真正的追随者和粉丝群，成千上万的人在观看和分享他所有的视频和帖子，这变成了一种病毒式的现象。

sentences.en: But beyond engaging on social media, people actually want to join in.
sentences.zh: 但除了在社交媒体上互动，人们实际上还想参与进来。

sentences.zh: 人们开始想要代表它，要求买衬衫，要求买贴纸。

sentences.zh: 所以我们制作了海报和传单，以进一步传播这个消息。

sentences.en: And it kind of became this...
sentences.zh: 它变得有点像……

sentences.zh: 彼得和他的朋友们销售“鸟类不是真的”周边商品。

sentences.zh: 比如 T 恤、卫衣、帽子、贴纸。

sentences.zh: 上面有鸟类的图片和写着“观鸟是双向的”之类的文字。

sentences.zh: 2018 年，他退学全职做这件事。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.zh: 他的粉丝更像是某种运动的追随者。

sentences.en: And that movement became known as the Bird Brigade.
sentences.zh: 那场运动被称为“鸟类旅”。

sentences.en: The movement goes from hundreds of people to thousands of people to tens of thousands of people to hundreds of thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 这场运动从数百人发展到数千人，再到数万人，最后是数十万人。

sentences.en: They even form chapters on college campuses across the country.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至在全国各地的大学校园里成立了分部。

sentences.en: And they host meetups.
sentences.zh: 他们举办聚会。

sentences.en: They wear their birds aren't real merchandise to football games.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着“鸟类不是真的”的周边去参加橄榄球比赛。

sentences.en: And they just kind of hang out.
sentences.zh: 他们只是聚在一起。

sentences.en: It's almost like a social club.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像一个社交俱乐部。

sentences.en: And over the last year or so, the Bird Brigade has really begun to mobilize for street protests.
sentences.zh: 在过去一年左右的时间里，“鸟类旅”已经真正开始动员起来进行街头抗议。

sentences.en: Things like that silly Twitter rally that I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 就像我提到的那个愚蠢的推特集会一样。

sentences.en: But also getting involved with more serious issues.
sentences.zh: 但也参与了一些更严肃的问题。

sentences.en: What kind of serious issues?
sentences.zh: 什么样严肃的问题？

sentences.en: Well, Peter told me that the Bird Brigade has started to actively show up at protests that have nothing to do with birds at all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，彼得告诉我，“鸟类旅”已经开始积极出现在与鸟类完全无关的抗议活动中。

sentences.en: He described a scene last year at the University of Cincinnati where an anti-abortion protest was taking place.
sentences.zh: 他描述了去年在辛辛那提大学发生的一幕，当时那里正在进行反堕胎抗议。

sentences.en: There was a group of anti-abortion activists that came out in full force shortly after the Texas abortion ban.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州堕胎禁令出台后不久，有一群反堕胎活动人士倾巢而出。

sentences.en: And were walking around with images of like mutilated babies.
sentences.zh: 他们走来走去，拿着残缺婴儿的照片。

sentences.en: And like, it was just very violent.
sentences.zh: 这非常暴力。

sentences.en: The Bird Brigade chapter at the university was watching this happen and decided to get involved.
sentences.zh: 该大学的“鸟类旅”分部目睹了这一切，决定介入。

sentences.en: They went and stood next to the anti-abortion people and basically held a mirror up to the absurdity.
sentences.zh: 他们走过去站在反堕胎人士旁边，基本上是给这种荒谬行为照了一面镜子。

sentences.en: And started, yeah, chanting Birds Aren't Real, which ultimately, shortly, turned the whole situation into a Birds Aren't Real rally.
sentences.zh: 然后开始高喊“鸟类不是真的”，最终，很快，整个局面变成了一场“鸟类不是真的”集会。

sentences.en: And we just got sent videos.
sentences.zh: 我们只是收到了视频。

sentences.en: They ended up kind of taking over the anti-abortion proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们最终接管了反堕胎抗议活动。

sentences.en: There was just sort of this like cacophony of comedy and absurdism that seemed to diffuse the anti-abortion people.
sentences.zh: 那儿出现了一种喜剧和荒诞的喧嚣，似乎化解了反堕胎人士的攻势。

sentences.en: And ultimately they had to just walk away because they couldn't even be heard.
sentences.zh: 最终他们不得不离开，因为他们甚至无法被听到。

sentences.en: So they went into the situation that was intense, confrontational, and non-aggressively diffused the harm that was being done through comedy, which is really interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以他们进入了一个紧张、对抗的局面，并通过喜剧非侵略性地化解了正在造成的伤害，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I don't know, I think Birds Aren't Real kind of like accidentally invented a new form of counter-protesting.

sentences.en: So Taylor, it's clear that Birds Aren't Real has become something much bigger than just a funny internet joke.
sentences.zh: 所以泰勒，很明显“鸟类不是真的”已经不仅仅是一个有趣的互联网笑话了。

sentences.en: It's actually mobilizing its followers to go out onto the street.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是在动员追随者走上街头。

sentences.en: But I guess I'm wondering why.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇为什么。

sentences.en: Why does Peter think that so many young people have found it so compelling?
sentences.zh: 为什么彼得认为这么多年轻人觉得它如此引人入胜？

sentences.en: Well, first off, I do think that some people just find it funny and entertaining.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我确实认为有些人只是觉得它很有趣、很娱乐。

sentences.en: But in talking with Peter, I also think that there's something more going on here that has a lot to do with the world that Gen Z has come up in.
sentences.zh: 但在与彼得交谈时，我也认为这里面还有更深层的东西，这与 Z 世代成长的世界有很大关系。

sentences.en: Why do you think people are drawn to it?
sentences.zh: 你认为人们为什么会被它吸引？

sentences.en: Tell me what you think, you know, what about Birds Aren't Real appeals to people?
sentences.zh: 告诉我你的想法，你知道，“鸟类不是真的”吸引人的地方是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's been so fascinating figuring that out because, like, people will come to these rallies in the hundreds.
sentences.zh: 是的，弄清楚这一点非常迷人，因为人们会成百上千地来参加这些集会。

sentences.en: And I think that in some ways it almost operates as, like, a safe space for people.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，它几乎成了人们的一个避风港。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I feel like every day I, like, wake up and open my phone,
sentences.zh: 我觉得每天我醒来打开手机，

sentences.en: I'm just seeing chaos.
sentences.zh: 我看到的只有混乱。

sentences.en: You know, I think just kind of growing up alongside the internet, just like, you know, Gen Z or anyone my age has, just kind of, like, grown up alongside it the whole time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为只是伴随着互联网成长，就像 Z 世代或任何我这个年纪的人一样，一直以来都是伴随着它成长的。

sentences.en: And with that, there's no real rules as a society of how to, like, deal with something like the internet.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是，作为一个社会，对于如何处理互联网这样的东西，并没有真正的规则。

sentences.en: So I think with that just comes, like, all the madness is in our face at once.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为随之而来的是，所有的疯狂都同时呈现在我们面前。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people feel the madness and don't really have a way to express it.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多人感受到了这种疯狂，却找不到表达的方式。

sentences.en: And so Birds Aren't Real, this satirical art project, provides a way for them to understand what feels like a world gone mad.
sentences.zh: 所以“鸟类不是真的”这个讽刺艺术项目，为他们提供了一种理解这个看似疯狂的世界的方式。

sentences.en: Okay, this might not be a good metaphor, but I feel like Birds Aren't Real is almost like an igloo in a snowstorm,
sentences.zh: 好吧，这可能不是一个好的比喻，但我觉得“鸟类不是真的”几乎就像暴风雪中的冰屋，

sentences.en: if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 如果这说得通的话。

sentences.en: Like, it's kind of like a place where people can kind of, like, make shelter out of the same type of material that's causing the chaos,
sentences.zh: 就像是一个人们可以利用造成混乱的同类材料来搭建避难所的地方，

sentences.en: given that, like, people can take misinformation and use it as a place to safely process misinformation.
sentences.zh: 鉴于人们可以利用错误信息，并将其作为一个安全处理错误信息的地方。

sentences.en: I think comedy is a very disarming form of communication.
sentences.zh: 我认为喜剧是一种非常能消除戒心的交流形式。

sentences.en: And it allows people to come together and laugh at these things that in everyday life are terrifying.
sentences.zh: 它让人们聚在一起，嘲笑那些在日常生活中令人恐惧的事情。

sentences.en: And there's something about laughing at these things that kind of, like, breaks the illusion of the monster.
sentences.zh: 嘲笑这些事情有一种打破怪物幻觉的作用。

sentences.en: And so I think young people have kind of coalesced around it because it's a way to kind of fight and poke fun at the conspiracy takeover of the world at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为年轻人之所以团结在它周围，是因为这是一种既能战斗又能同时嘲弄世界上阴谋论泛滥的方式。

sentences.en: It feels like a mirror.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像一面镜子。

sentences.en: Even just from the first day that it started, it was just kind of a mirror to what everybody was feeling then.
sentences.zh: 即使从它开始的第一天起，它就只是当时每个人感受的一面镜子。

sentences.en: I think it still operates in a similar way.
sentences.zh: 我认为它仍然以类似的方式运作。

sentences.en: And, yeah, I think that that reflection can be used, like, you know, for coping and therapeutic purposes just through the satire
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我认为这种反思可以通过讽刺，

sentences.en: and through kind of these, like, rallies that we hold.
sentences.zh: 以及我们举办的这些集会，用于应对和治疗目的。
